source.title: Similarity of Neural Network Models: A Survey of Functional and Representational Measures
source.authors: Max Klabunde; Tobias Schumacher; M. Strohmaier; Florian Lemmerich

record.tranche_reason: The survey's own synthetic experiment shows that Orthogonal Procrustes scores vary with representation dimensionality, refining how measured similarity scores should be interpreted. Other empirical findings discussed are cited from prior work.
record.gate_note: The only own result bearing on the claim is the synthetic Orthogonal Procrustes dimensionality experiment in Figure 5 and Appendix F. Other results about convergence, metric comparisons, or input dependence are summaries of cited studies, not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a survey of similarity measures. It does not test whether model representations converge. Its own result is a synthetic demonstration: Orthogonal Procrustes distance between random matrices (Gaussian, not model activations) grows with dimensionality D until D=N. That is a property of a measure, not a measurement of how much trained models converge, so it bears on no version. V6 needs measured convergence between models to shift with the measure, settings or inputs. All findings on model universality, disagreement between measures and input dependence (Ding et al., Brown et al., Cui et al., Jones et al., ReSi) are cited from other work.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that research on the properties and applicability of representational similarity measures is lacking. They note that different measures can give materially different results and no measure stands out across existing tests. Scores need context, since inputs and factors like dimensionality affect them. Their Appendix F demo illustrates the dimensionality point.
record.recipe_differences: No reproduction of the original sources' methods; this is a survey, with an additional synthetic Orthogonal Procrustes dimensionality demonstration.
record.method_sensitivity: Orthogonal Procrustes scores vary with representation dimensionality; the text states that scores rise until D=N and then remain flat.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic random matrices (N=1000), Orthogonal Procrustes distance rises with D as a power law until D=N, then stays flat. This holds for both rotated-plus-noise pairs and a shuffled-row baseline of unrelated matrices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The raw scale of a representational similarity measure depends on representation dimensionality, so scores across models of different width need normalising or baselines before convergence is compared.

record.problems: The own experiment uses synthetic random matrices rather than trained models, and reports its score curves only in a figure without tabulated values. It addresses dimensionality dependence, not model convergence with scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Findings summarized from other papers are cited results and are not extracted as this survey's own results.

untested.parts: Convergence with scale or capability across architectures, objectives and data is not tested; it is only cited (Section 5).
Vision–language alignment is only cited (Maniparambil et al.); not tested.
Seed-to-seed convergence is only cited (layer-matching tests, Mehrer et al., Li et al.); not tested.
Stitching, linear maps and relative representations are described as measures, not tested.
Universal features or circuits are not tested.
Metric, hyperparameter and input dependence of measured model similarity is argued from cited work (Appendix C, Table 3). The own experiment uses synthetic matrices, not models.
Partial convergence and its causes are only cited (e.g. partial similarity, functional differences across seeds).

record.verdict_notes: Survey (ACM Computing Surveys). The reader's V6 'tested' and limits_scope label are removed. The synthetic experiment concerns a measure's score range, not model convergence, and V6 is about measured model alignment. Researchers interested in V6 should follow the cited primary studies the survey summarises: Ding et al. 2021, Brown et al. 2024 on OOD inputs, Cui et al. 2022, Jones et al. 2022, Davari et al. 2022, and the ReSi benchmark (Klabunde et al. 2024).

versions.untested_parts: The survey reviews cited findings about model universality but does not itself test convergence with model scale, capability, architecture, objective, or data.
Cross-modal alignment of paired images and captions as models improve is not tested.
Convergent learning across seeds is discussed through cited work, not tested with the survey's own results.
The survey reviews alignment and mapping measures but does not itself test interchangeability.
Recurring interpretable features or circuits are not tested.

The own experiment tests Orthogonal Procrustes score sensitivity to representation dimensionality on synthetic data. It does not test alternative similarity measures, neighbour settings, input datasets, or OOD inputs.
The survey mentions cited findings on partial representational similarity and functional differences, but does not itself test whether alignment plateaus or is caused by shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: synthetic representation matrices
rows.operation_detail: Measured Orthogonal Procrustes distance between a random matrix and its orthogonally transformed copy with added Gaussian noise.
rows.baseline: Shuffled-row baseline is shown as a reference; value figure only
rows.uncertainty: Mean over ten repetitions for each D; standard deviation is too small to be visible
rows.note: The text states that scores increase with dimensionality until D=N, then remain flat. The noise SD is varied; the baseline does not depend on noise.
rows.check: Subject is synthetic Gaussian matrices and their rotated, noised copies, not representations of trained models. It shows the Procrustes distance scale depends on D, not that measured model convergence depends on the metric. Figure only, no tabulated values.
